t: London was founded by the Romans about 47 CE and was destroyed by Boudica's Iceni within about fifteen years, then rebuilt as a planned town.
After a post-Roman decline it revived inside its old walls from 886, and from 1066 it was the place where England's kings were crowned and where government settled at Westminster.
Plague in 1665 and 1666 and the Great Fire of 1666 struck the old city, and from the 19th century it grew into the world's largest city, with 6.7 million people in 1900.
dyk: In 1666 the Great Fire destroyed about 60 per cent of London, including 87 parish churches, yet it is believed to have cost at most 16 lives.

f.founded: By the Romans as Londinium, about 47 CE, some four years after their invasion of 43 CE; no Iron Age town has been found on the site
f.where: On the River Thames in south-east England, at the river's lowest bridging point, in England, United Kingdom
f.known: The Roman wall and Londinium; the Tower of London; Westminster Abbey and the Palace of Westminster; the Great Fire of 1666; St Paul's Cathedral; London Bridge; the East India Company; the Blitz
f.today: The capital of England and the United Kingdom, a metropolis around the historic City of London.
